header: INTERACTIVE · TELEGRAPH RELAY ·· DISCRETE SYMBOLS, REGENERATED AT EACH RELAY
INTERACTIVE · TELEGRAPH RELAY ·· ANALOG AMPLIFIED, REGENERATED AT EACH RELAY
note: An electromechanical relay along the line didn't need to pass the wave itself; it only needed to detect whether a pulse was present, and then recreate a brand new, clean copy of that pulse to send down the next segment of wire.
Now the relays merely boost what arrives (like an analog amplifier). It cannot distinguish a pulse from noise, so it boosts the noise along with the signal, until Baltimore misreads the message.
